scenes.brief: Commissioning week. FIC-101 (feed flow controller on FV-101) keeps oscillating because the upstream feed composition swings. Dana decides to deliberately detune FIC-101 for now rather than chase it. Luis asks if operators should expect sluggish feed response and Dana says yes, that is intentional. Priya makes the tuning change.
Pure shift chatter: who covers Saturday, a coffee machine complaint, a reminder about hard hats in the new unit. Nothing technical.

Morning of the incident. P-102A tripped and smells burnt; Mark found the mechanical seal failed. Luis says V-102 was drained empty overnight: LV-202 went fully open during an instrument air pressure dip and emptied the drum, then P-102A ran dry. Dana says come get her, she is heading down, and tells them to run P-102B and keep V-102 level up manually.

Follow-up. Dana confirms root cause: seal failed from dry running after LV-202 failed open on the air dip. Priya confirms the air header dipped. Hannah says there will be an incident review meeting and an MOC for corrective actions. They agree a low-low level protection on the reflux pumps is needed.

MOC-2019-021 review. Changes: add low-low level trip LSLL-202 on both reflux pumps (P-102A and P-102B), add check valves CV-102A and CV-102B on the pump discharges, and add a low-flow alarm FAL-201. Hannah asks about proof testing, Luis asks what operators will see when the trip fires. Approved, drawing goes to Rev 1.
Chatter about a contractor parking issue, a forklift near-miss reminder, and the cafeteria menu. Nothing technical.

MOC-2020-014: upsize the trim on FV-201 (reflux control valve) from Cv 45 to Cv 75 because the plant is moving to higher feed rates and the old trim runs out of range. Hannah asks about noise and cavitation, Dana says it is fine at the new rates. Priya will update the valve datasheet. Approved, Rev 2.

Since the FV-201 trim change, the valve hunts whenever the unit runs below about 40% load. Luis says operators now put FIC-201 in manual below 40% and nudge it by hand. Dana says that is a known side effect of the bigger trim and not worth another change right now.

Mark says the P-102A seal was replaced again, work order WO-71120. He suspects shaft misalignment this time, not dry running. Dana agrees it looks like alignment and says make P-102B the preferred duty pump and keep P-102A as standby. Luis updates the operator notes.

Hannah mentions that after the inspection group re-evaluated the column MAWP, PSV-201 set pressure was lowered from 17.2 to 16.5 barg. Priya asks whether the PSV datasheet in Drive has been updated, Hannah says she has not gotten to it yet. Dana says just remember the drawing still says 17.2 until someone fixes it. Do NOT mention approvals, MOC or paperwork for the change.
Chatter: a lunch order, shift swap request, a forklift beeping complaint. Nothing technical.

E-101 (feed/bottoms exchanger) is fouling and feed temperature to the column is sagging. Luis says operators keep chasing it. Dana says she will propose a bypass around E-101 so they can hold feed temperature between cleanings. Mark says cleanings are expensive so a bypass buys time.

MOC-2022-007: add bypass valve BV-101 around E-101 to hold feed temperature as the exchanger fouls. Hannah asks about overheating downstream, Dana says operators open it partially and watch the bottoms temperature. Approved, drawing goes to Rev 3.

Evening shift tripped TAH-301, the high-temperature alarm on the storage tank, after opening BV-101 all the way. Luis explains that with the bypass open the bottoms run hotter on their way to storage, and TAH-301 trips at 55 C. Dana says never fully open BV-101, only crack it and watch the storage temperature. Mark says he will add a note to the operator sheet.

MOC-2023-009: relocate TT-203 from tray 28 to tray 32 and raise TIC-203 setpoint from 78 to 81 C, with a loop retune. Hannah asks if the new setpoint stays inside product spec, Dana says yes. Approved, Rev 4.

After moving TT-203 to tray 32, Priya says the old tray 28 reading was insensitive, which is why they moved it; the new location responds much faster. She finished the retune of TIC-203 and the loop is stable at 81 C. Dana says good, tell Luis's crew the old setpoint was 78 in case they see it in old notes.
Chatter: summer heat, a broken break-room fridge, a reminder about a safety stand-down. Nothing technical.

Mark says E-101 was cleaned last week. He reminds everyone the cleaning interval is about 18 months and the last cleaning before this one was why BV-101 had been open so much. Luis says feed temperature is back to normal and BV-101 is closed again.

Near-miss during startup. Luis says V-102 nearly overfilled because LIC-202 was left in manual and nobody caught it until the high level alarm. Mark says he saw level climbing and called it in. They agree nobody was hurt and nothing was released, but it was close. Luis says there will be a review.

Review of the near-miss. Dana says LV-202 currently fails open, which is part of why the drum can overfill when the controller is out of the loop. She proposes changing LV-202 to fail closed, accepting the overfill risk because the high-level alarm covers it. Hannah wants it done under an MOC. Priya will check the actuator.

MOC-2024-031: change LV-202 fail position from fail-open to fail-closed. The overfill risk is accepted and covered by the high-level alarm. Luis asks how operators will know the valve closed on loss of air. Approved, drawing goes to Rev 5.

During a preventive maintenance round Priya found the LV-202 actuator is still set up fail-open, even though the drawing and the MOC say fail-closed. She raised work order WO-88213 to fix it. Dana says that should have been done when the MOC closed and asks Priya to chase it. The conversation ends with no one confirming it got done.
Mostly chatter and scheduling. Somewhere in it Mark says the steam trap on E-103 is not great but has never failed, so he is not planning to touch it. Do not explain why or give any sizing.

A new operator asked Luis about starting the reflux pumps. Dana repeats her rule: never start either P-102 pump unless V-102 level is at least 30%. Luis says he will add it to the startup checklist. Dana mentions she is putting together handover notes in Drive before she retires.

Dana's last day. Warm farewell chatter. Luis thanks her, Mark jokes about her rules of thumb, Priya says the handover notes are in Drive but she knows they are not complete. Dana says ask Priya and Luis, they know where things are buried. No new technical facts.
